title: Braised Cabbage with Apple
subtitle: Slow-braised white cabbage with apple, vinegar, and spices
excerpt: White cabbage braised low and slow with apple, red wine vinegar, honey, and warm spices. A sweet-sour side dish that works well with pork and game.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from British and German braised cabbage traditions. Long slow cooking softens the cabbage and allows the sweet-sour balance to develop.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water. The flavour improves the next day.

content.text: Keep the heat low and the lid on for most of the cooking. The cabbage braises in the moisture it releases.
Melt the butter in a large, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the shredded cabbage and sliced apple. Stir to mix with the onion.
Add the red wine vinegar, honey, cinnamon, and cloves. Season with salt and a little pepper. Stir well.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Remove the lid for the final 5 minutes. The liquid should mostly have evaporated and the cabbage should be tender and glossy.
Remove the whole cloves. Taste and adjust with a little more honey or vinegar as needed.

items.symptom: Cabbage is catching on the bottom of the pot.
items.cause: Heat was too high or lid not fitted tightly.
items.fix: Use a very low heat and a tight-fitting lid; stir more often.

items.symptom: Cabbage is watery and not glossy.
items.cause: Lid left on too long in the final stage.
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 5 to 10 minutes to reduce the liquid.

items.cause: Vinegar not balanced by enough honey.
items.fix: Add another teaspoon of honey and taste again.
